interpretation_limits: left_servo_ns/right_servo_ns are wall-clock durations, not CPU execution times. Their intervals may span the watchdog stop timestamp and include contention or scheduling after stopping began. Do not treat their whole durations as pre-stop CPU computation or independent proof that IK CPU work caused the stop.

The sum-based servo end time is an estimate from executor start plus two measured durations; Python overhead between measurements is excluded. It is useful for budget comparison, not an exact completion timestamp.

cycle.elapsed_ns, cycle.executor_ns and rejected driver_submit_ns can include stop/cleanup and exception propagation; do not equate them to normal-cycle computation or successful native submission latency.

last_native_call describes the last recorded native call associated with the previously accepted target. A current rejected driver_submit wall time is not evidence that a new tj_submit native call took that long.

50 minus old_target_remaining_at_accept is an inferred prior creation-to-accept latency only if the prior target used a 50ms creation-based expiry and deadline equals that expiry. The source code must establish those assumptions.
preceding_sdk_wall_timestamp is the preceding timestamped SDK warning, not the exact wall-clock time of the pause. Monotonic timestamps in each event are the timing evidence.
Ready/fresh input and feedback snapshots at these events do not prove that every component was healthy at every earlier time. The JSON has no CPU profiling or scheduling breakdown.
Hardware Stall/Enc1BitRate warnings and exit-adjacent ADB stream termination messages occur in the same log, but temporal coexistence alone does not establish that they caused the 13 watchdog pauses.

performance_audit.scope: No hardware opened, started, engaged or commanded; project files unchanged. Real local Tianji FK/Jacobian and CartesianServo are called.

measurement.target: Ready joints from tests/test_tianji_servo.py; original FK pose translated +3,+2,+1 mm. Proposals repeated without accept; this is fixed-case timing, not a trajectory replay.
measurement.timers: perf_counter_ns wall time and thread_time_ns CPU time; stage wrappers add some overhead
measurement.thread_sched: Benchmark proposals run continuously; simulated receive threads use production receive/drain/decode paths; no real SDK receive/network/Quest/hand retarget/publish call/stop callbacks.
measurement.feedback: 1000 Hz synthetic dual-arm packet; actual driver._receive drains up to256 then waits2ms
measurement.feedback_wuji: Plus two WujiHandDriver._receive threads, each500Hz joints+100Hz diagnostics
measurement.feedback_wuji_1k: Plus two WujiHandDriver._receive threads, each1000Hz joints+1000Hz diagnostics; assumed pressure condition, not observed hardware frequency
measurement.feedback_periodic: Plus artificial pure-Python2.5ms busy burst+2.5ms wait, a synthetic50-percent GIL load, not a hardware replica.
measurement.limitations: Synthetic frames lack native object property cost. Background OS processes and CPU frequency not controlled. Results demonstrate possible wall-time amplification but do not uniquely attribute the observed stops.

receiver_microbenchmark.method: Actual Python receiver processing with reused synthetic packets, no native receive/subscription or transport; includes sequence/stamp updates. Microbenchmark only.

import sys, time, json
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace as NS
sys.path.insert(0, '/home/yuchen/project/bimanual-teleop')
import numpy as np
import wuji_sdk
from tests.test_tianji import packet
from tests.test_wuji_driver import feedback, diagnostics
from bimanual_teleop.devices.tianji.driver import TianjiDriver
from bimanual_teleop.devices.wuji.adapter import WujiHandDriver
from bimanual_teleop.types import ControlProfile

def measure(fn, n=5000):
    wall=[]; cpu=[]
    for i in range(n):
        w=time.perf_counter_ns();c=time.thread_time_ns()
        fn(i)
        cpu.append(time.thread_time_ns()-c);wall.append(time.perf_counter_ns()-w)
    return {'wall_ms_p50_p99_max':(np.percentile(wall,[50,99,100])/1e6).tolist(),
            'thread_cpu_ms_p50_p99_max':(np.percentile(cpu,[50,99,100])/1e6).tolist()}

t=TianjiDriver('offline-synthetic');t.profile=NS(active_arms=('left','right'));t.engaged=True;t._mode_confirmed=False
p=packet()
def arm(i):
    p.packet_index=i;p.sequence[:]=(i,i);p.received_ns=time.monotonic_ns()
    t._on_feedback(p)
h=WujiHandDriver('left','offline-synthetic',sdk=wuji_sdk)
state=feedback();diag=diagnostics(enabled=True);warning=diagnostics(enabled=True,code=7)
def hand(stream,frame,i):
    frame.header.seq=i;h._consume(stream,frame,time.monotonic_ns())
out={'hardware_access':False,'method':'Actual Python receiver processing with reused synthetic packets, no native receive/subscription or transport; includes sequence/stamp updates. Microbenchmark only.',
     'tianji_on_feedback':measure(arm),
     'wuji_joints_fake_frame':measure(lambda i:hand('joints',state,i)),
     'wuji_diagnostics_fake_frame':measure(lambda i:hand('diagnostics',diag,i)),
     'wuji_diagnostics_20_warnings_fake_frame':measure(lambda i:hand('diagnostics',warning,i+5000)),
     'warning_severity':{str(code):wuji_sdk.WujiHand2.describe_error(code) for code in (3,7)}}
Path('/tmp/teleop_receiver_microbench_20260915.json').write_text(json.dumps(out,indent=2))
print(json.dumps(out,indent=2))
